judgments.catchwords: CIVIL PROCEDURE - Written submissions - Filing outside extended time without further application - Retrospective extension - Appellant afforded adequate opportunity to reply - No fresh evidence introduced - Fairness and prejudice - Whether late submissions should be admitted - Rules of Court 2012, O 3 r 5. DAMAGES - Personal injuries - Road traffic accident - Appeal on quantum - Medical expenses paid by insurer - Insurance benefits exception to rule against recovery of loss already made good - Whether tortfeasors entitled to benefit from injured person’s insurance arrangement - Whether direct payment to hospital affected recovery - Award substituted with proven expenses of RM141,403.95. DAMAGES - Special damages - Travelling expenses for medical attendances - Full amount claimed insufficiently proved - Reasonable award of RM3,000 - Past loss of earnings – Employer’s evidence of 109 unpaid days of certified medical leave - Whether subsequent resignation extinguished accrued salary loss - Whether deduction for living expenses appropriate - Award substituted with RM13,778.69. DAMAGES - Future medical expenses - Ankle-foot orthosis and special footwear - General pleading of future medical expenses - Quotation tendered and witnesses cross-examined without unfair surprise or prejudice - Whether pleading objection could defeat claim - Necessity assessed with specialist evidence - RM93,200 allowed - Increased claim for price escalation insufficiently proved - Future treatment and surgery - Substantial possibility or likelihood of future loss supported by cogent evidence - Competing medical opinions - Award of RM58,840 affirmed. DAMAGES - Loss of future earnings - Loss of earning capacity - Distinction - Permanent lower-limb impairment restricting former occupation involving travel and site visits - Capacity for sedentary employment - Unemployment alone insufficient to prove continuing loss of future earnings - Real or substantial risk of disadvantage in labour market - Future earnings claim dismissed - Lump sum of RM80,000 awarded for loss of earning capacity - Appeal allowed in part.

judgments.title: HENG CHEW LANG & ors v TOPGAN REAL ESTATE SDN BHD & ors
judgments.catchwords: LAND LAW - Indefeasibility of title - Transfers executed under invalid powers of attorney - Donors not present before authenticating solicitor - Attorney lacking authority to execute Forms 14A - Transfers constituting insufficient or void instruments - Immediate transferees acquiring title directly from registered proprietors through purported attorney - Whether genuine purchase, valuable consideration and absence of personal fraud protected immediate transferees - Titles defeasible - Proviso protecting qualifying subsequent purchasers inapplicable - National Land Code 1965, ss 340(2)(b) and 340(3). POWERS OF ATTORNEY - Execution and authentication - Statutory requirement of execution before authorised person - Immigration records and oral evidence contradicting certified attendance - Genuineness of signatures not establishing compliance - Registration, asserted consideration and description as irrevocable not curing invalid execution - Powers invalid insofar as they concerned plaintiffs’ interests - Powers of Attorney Act 1949, s 3(1)(a). TRUSTS - Resulting trust - Alleged sole provision of purchase money - Family business proceeds passing through claimant’s personal account - Absence of coherent property-by-property tracing of contributions at acquisition - Subsequent expenditure and management insufficient without more to establish beneficial ownership from inception - Resulting-trust counterclaim dismissed. EVIDENCE - Burden of proof - Challenge to execution of powers of attorney - Plaintiffs retaining legal burden to establish statutory defect on balance of probabilities - Documents marked for identification not evidence of truth of contents - Neither side entitled to treat disputed recitals as proved - Invalid execution established through independent admitted evidence and oral testimony - Evidence Act 1950, ss 101 and 102. CIVIL PROCEDURE - Issue estoppel - Earlier removal of private caveats - Whether validity of execution and authentication necessarily and finally adjudicated - Removal order not by its operative effect alone establishing valid authority or indefeasible title - Asserted estoppel not established. REMEDIES - Cancellation and restoration of registered interests - Relief confined to plaintiffs’ proved interests - Independently valid interests and terms of bank settlements preserved - Personal fraud and conspiracy against purchasers not proved - Additional damages not sufficiently proved – Attorney’s resulting-trust counterclaim and purchaser’s counterclaim dismissed.

judgments.catchwords: The Court of Appeal reaffirmed the principle of minimal judicial intervention in arbitration. A procedural breach, such as an alleged one-day delay in submitting a draft award for AIAC technical review, does not automatically invalidate an arbitral award where the requirement is merely directory, no timely objection was raised, and no prejudice is shown. An arbitral award will not be set aside on the basis of a purported “new difference” where the issue was within the parties’ pleadings, evidence and submissions. Courts will not review the merits of an award under the guise of a setting-aside application.’
